subject.title: Feature Request: Disable exec command credential masking / secret replacement

question: Should OpenClaw allow trusted operators to disable forced tool/exec safety-surface redaction, and if so should that be a narrow scoped opt-in or only a parser/display exemption?
rationale: The requested behavior changes credential exposure boundaries and adds config surface; source inspection does not prove the reported shell-command mutation, so automation cannot choose the security/product tradeoff safely.

options.title: Keep forced redaction pending repro
options.body: Keep safety-boundary redaction mandatory and ask for an exact live command/output trace before considering any new opt-out.

options.title: Approve a narrow trusted opt-in
options.body: Define a documented, explicit trusted-operator opt-in for specific tool-payload surfaces with tests, docs, and audit guidance.

options.title: Limit to parser/display exemption
options.body: If the failure is only approval/display parsing, preserve redaction but exempt the confirmed quoted or heredoc case without adding a global bypass.

recommendation.title: Keep forced redaction pending repro
recommendation.body: Keep safety-boundary redaction mandatory and ask for an exact live command/output trace before considering any new opt-out.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged redaction expansion is the closest current-main ownership signal for forced tool payload and approval display redaction.
